results.summary_before: multimac is a multi-use accelerator that computes vector dot products, minimums, and maximums on 4-bit data. It operates as a coprocessor, loading data via index and data pins and executing when run is asserted, producing a 12-bit result after at least 16 clock cycles. The design was tested using Verilator simulation with a C++ workbench, focusing on numerical stability. It is intended to be driven by an RP2040 for vector calculations.

results.summary_before: LISA is an 8-bit microcontroller SoC with 128 bytes of DFFRAM, designed for embedded control. It includes a BrainFloat16 FPU, timers, GPIO, UART, SPI/QSPI, and I2C master, and can interface with external flash and RAM. A C-based toolchain (assembler, linker, C compiler) and a Python debugger are provided, though the C compiler is incomplete and buggy. Silicon testing confirmed the core, debugger, DFFRAM, SPI/QSPI, FPU, timers, GPIO, and UART, but I2C and the DFFRAM cache controller remain untested.

results.summary_before: This is a hardware processor for the esoteric Brainfuck language, implementing 75% of the instruction set (excluding I/O operations). It uses an external address register and requires separate program and data memories of at least 256x8 each, expandable to 1KB. The design is intended to be driven with a clock up to 20 MHz and can interface with SRAM, ROM, and LED bars for output. The documentation includes a state machine diagram and pinout but no silicon test results.

results.summary_before: This is an 8-bit R2R digital-to-analog converter with an optional sawtooth waveform generator. It can be driven externally via digital inputs or by the internal generator, and the analog output is on a single pin. Testing requires a multimeter to measure the output voltage. Silicon tests confirm it works, with one tester observing a sawtooth at ~600 mV and frequencies up to 1 MHz.
